en: The Record of Items Brought Back from Yuezhou by Daisōjō (Saichō), Master of the Propagation of the Teachings,
titled "Catalogue of the Japanese Monk Saichō’s Quest for the Dharma," comprises a total of two hundred and thirty works in four hundred and sixty fascicles.
I obtained the titles of one hundred twenty-eight works in three hundred forty-five fascicles from Taizhou; their specific names are detailed in a separate record.
From Yuefu, I secured the original manuscripts to transcribe the scriptures and the liturgical manuals for recitation.
In total, there are one hundred and two sections comprising one hundred and fifteen fascicles:
the *Five Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Cakra-Vartin Sūtra* in five fascicles (one hundred sheets); the *Mahācakra-Vajra Dhāraṇī Sūtra* in one fascicle;
the *Sūtra of the Woman Who Constantly Seeks Profit and Poison* in one fascicle; the *Separate Translation of the Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā* in one fascicle; and the *Khaṇḍaroṭaka*... [text truncated].
*Li púsà fǎ* (Rituals for the Bodhisattva Li), one fascicle; *Jùntuólì biéfǎ* (Separate Rituals for Kuntali), one fascicle; *Qiúhèi* (Guhya), three fascicles;

*Wúliàngshòu rúlái yúqié yíguǐ* (Yoga Rite of the Tathāgata Amitāyus), one fascicle; *Èrshíwǔméizīdǐnglúnwáng yúqié fǎ* (Yoga Method of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King of the Twenty-five Seals), one fascicle;
*Púxián jīngāng yúqié fǎ* (Vajra Yoga Method of Samantabhadra), one fascicle; *Shíbāhuì yúqié fǎ* (Yoga Method of the Eighteen Assemblies), one fascicle; *Pǔ...* [text fragment].
*The Praise of the Worthy One’s Vows and Aspirations*, one fascicle; *The Names of the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle; *The Essential Heart of the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle;
*The Praise of the Vajra of the Ratna Family*, one fascicle; *The Dharma of Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle; *The Vinaya Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*The Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra in Sanskrit Characters*, one fascicle; *The Vajracakra Dhāraṇī in Sanskrit and Chinese Characters*, one fascicle.
One fascicle of the *Jueduoluoni qingqingwen* (Petition for the Invocation of the Vidyārājñī Dhāraṇī). The above twenty works, totaling twenty-six fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

One fascicle of the *Dadueluonijing* (Mahādhāraṇīsūtra); one fascicle of the *Fantian zhedijing* (Brahmadeva-bhūmiparīkṣāsūtra); and one fascicle of the *Zamiyan* (Miscellaneous Mantras) in the Han [language].
*Uṣṇīṣa-samaya-śīla*, one fascicle; *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-vijayā-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script, one fascicle;
*Maṇḍala-patterns*, one fascicle; *Patterns for the Thirty-seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle; *Patterns for the Ritual Implements of the Thirty-seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle;
*Combined Patterns for the Maṇḍala and Ritual Implements*, one fascicle; *Seals for Miscellaneous Ritual Implements*, one fascicle; *Dharmas of Vaiśravaṇa*, one fascicle.

One scroll on the iconography of the Golden Wheel Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa; one scroll on the Three Seals of the Single-Syllable Cakra-Vartin; one scroll on the iconography of the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas;
one scroll of the Single-Syllable Sanskrit characters; one scroll on the iconography of Vajra-Agneya; one scroll on the positions of the Eight Bodhisattvas;
one scroll on the ritual for the Unrestricted Feast for the Realm of the Dead; and one scroll on the ritual procedure for adding the *hūṃ* syllable of fire.
The first eighteen fascicles above comprise eighteen works in eighteen fascicles within the same volume.

*Sijiaoyi* (Meanings of the Four Teachings), two fascicles; Chapter Three and Chapter Four; "Epitaph for Master Zhi'an," one fascicle, composed by Shi Faxuan of Hongshan Temple in Changzhou, eight pages;

"Letter from Liang Su to the Daoist Wu Yun," one fascicle, three pages; and *Tiantai Zhizhe Dashi Biezhuan* (Separate Biography of the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai), one fascicle, compiled by Zhang’an Heshu. These two [works] follow.

*Preface to the Commentary on the *Mohe Zhiguan* (Ten Sheets), in one fascicle; composed by Pumenzi. *Preface to the Origins of the *Zhizhuan Shiqian*, in one fascicle; composed by Pumenzi, the son of Junshan Chujin.

*Stele for the Stone Image of Maitreya at Shicheng Temple on Mount Shan*, in one fascicle. *The Bequeathed Instructions of Upādhyāya Miaole*, in one fascicle. *Eulogy for Paintings of the Three Tathāgatas*, in one fascicle.

*Record of the Master Tiantai’s Practice of Reciting Sutras and Meditation*, in one fascicle. *Text for the Sacrificial Offering to the Sixth Patriarch, Upādhyāya Jingxi*, in one fascicle; composed by Upādhyāya Jingxi. [Endorsed] by the Tiantai Śramaṇa Lingyi.

One fascicle of *Notes on Divergent Meanings in the Commentary on the Śamatha-vipaśyanā*, compiled by the Seat-Master [Dao]xuan; one fascicle of the *Brief Biography of the Seventh Patriarch of Tiantai, Master Zhidu*, compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhiming;

one fascicle of the *Eulogy for the Late Master Jingxi of Fulong Mountain, Tang Dynasty*, composed by Shen’ung of Kuaiji; one fascicle of the *Miscellaneous Collection from Guoqing Temple of Tiantai*;

one fascicle of the *Record of the Shadow Hall of Master Zhiyi at Guoqing Temple*; one fascicle of the *Record of Mount Qingxi* by the Śramaṇa Tanyi of Chang’an; and the *Outline of Śamatha-vipaśyanā*.

*Wen* (Text), one fascicle; *Sijiao Wencun* (Excerpts from the Four Teachings), one fascicle; *Shi erbufa kewen* (Outline of the Ten Non-dual Sections), one fascicle; *Chang’an Zuozhu Zhuan* (Biography of the Chang’an Preceptor), one fascicle. Compiled by the Tiantai śramaṇa Qianji.
The above twenty-one works, totaling twenty-two fascicles, are contained in the same volume as the first section of the *Za* (Miscellaneous) collection, comprising thirty sheets.

*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-ṭīkā*, three fascicles, composed by the Śramaṇa Yuánhuī; *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-stūpa-inscription*, one fascicle, [composed at] Waguan Monastery; *Guānhé Wénbǐ*, one fascicle; *Dazhidu-lùn Yīn*, one fascicle; *Gōngjīn Fódào Lúnhéng*, two fascicles; *Wǔbǎi Wènsì*, one fascicle; *Zhēnrén Jí*, one fascicle. These seven works, totaling ten fascicles, constitute the second volume of the "Miscellaneous" section.

*Zhūxián Wèndá* (Questions and Answers of the Various Worthies), one fascicle; *Hànlin Yuàn Dìjí* (Collected Works of the Hanlin Academy), one fascicle; *Xīgù Fǔfǎ Jì* (Record of the Transmission of the Dharma in the Western Regions), one fascicle;

*Húzhōu Jiǎorán Héshàng Zhāiwén* (Farewell Texts of the Venerable Jiǎorán of Húzhōu), one fascicle; *Záwén Wǔshǒu* (Five Miscellaneous Essays), one fascicle; *Wéizhījìn Zhuàn* (Biography of Wéizhījìn), one fascicle;

*Fù Dàshì Huánshī Shí'èrshǒu* (Twelve Poems on Returning by the Great Being Fǔ), one fascicle; *Huáyán Fǎjiè Guān* (Contemplation of the Dharmadhātu of the Avataṃsaka), one fascicle; *Zhāi* (Farewell Texts), one fascicle.
*Wenshi* (Models of Literary Style), one fascicle; *Fouyou pian* (Chapter on Floating Bubbles), one fascicle; *Fudao erzong lun* (Treatise on the Two Schools of Buddhism and Daoism), one fascicle;

*Sanjiao buqi lun* (Treatise on the Unevenness of the Three Teachings), one fascicle; *Shizi zan* (Praise of the Ten Disciples), one fascicle; *Shi Fashi fufa* (The Dharma-Transmission of Master Kumārajīva), one fascicle; *Daotige* (Song of the Knife-Ladder), one fascicle;

*Jingxin si zhongming* (Inscription for the Bell of Jingxin Temple), one fascicle; *Wugeng zan nianfo* (Praise of Reciting the Buddha’s Name at the Fifth Watch), one fascicle; and *Pusa jie wenju* (Text and Phrases of the Bodhisattva Precepts).
One fascicle: *Treatise of the Great Master of the Western Regions*. One fascicle: *Treatise on Contemplating the Mind*. One fascicle: *Meaning of Non-arising*. One fascicle:
*Collection of the Great Being of the Twin Trees*, twenty sheets. One fascicle: *Biography of the Great Master of Caoxi*. One fascicle: *Treatise on Transcending Contemplation*.
One fascicle: *Names and Characteristics of the Lotus Sūtra*. One fascicle: *Dhāraṇī Method of the Blue-Faced Northern Heavenly Deity*. [One fascicle: *Prajñā*.
*Heart Sūtra Brief Commentary*, one fascicle; *Chart of the Dharma Lineage*, one fascicle; *Meaning of Resolving the Buddha’s Experience of Suffering*, one fascicle (fifteen sheets);
*Chapter on Dharmatā*, one fascicle; *Judgment on the Addition of Green [Ink]*, one fascicle (ten sheets); *The Two Meditative Concentrations and the Two Precept-Substances*, one fascicle;
*Numerical Meanings from the *Commentary on the Four-Part Vinaya***, one fascicle (twenty sheets); *Phonetics of the *Commentary on the Four-Part Vinaya***.
*Xiun* (Exhortation), one fascicle, fifteen sheets; *Daochangding* (Pinnacle of the Dharma Hall), one fascicle, missing.
The above thirty-four works, totaling thirty-four fascicles, are contained in the same bundle as the third section of the *Za* (Miscellaneous) collection, comprising sixty sheets.

One fascicle of the *General Catalogue of the Quest for the Dharma in the Japanese Kingdom* and four fascicles of the *Collection of Correspondence*, comprising seven parts (A–G) totaling one hundred sheets or more; these two works, totaling five fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The forms of the implements for recitation and offering are as follows: one five-pronged *vajra*, one five-pronged golden *vajra-bell*, two *vajra-wheels*, and two *vajra-karmas*. These, along with the three-pronged *vajra* which is the dharma-seal and token of transmission bestowed by the mantra-teacher (*mantra-upādhyāya*), constitute the aforementioned forms of the implements for recitation and offering.
The aforementioned dhāraṇī-recitation dharma-gates, along with the models for the implements used in recitation and offerings,
were sent to Yuefu Longxing Monastery to be presented to the Venerable Huishun.
Thereupon, Saichō and Gishin followed the Upādhyāya to the practice hall on the eastern peak of Lake Kōmyō.
The Upādhyāya led the two monks as they prepared the practice hall.
He was introduced to the maṇḍala altar of the five families of empowerment and was personally granted the dharma of mantras;
furthermore, he received the empowerment water of the mantras.
Saichō and his companions then transcribed the aforementioned dhāraṇī-recitation ritual manual along with the patterns for the ritual implements;
having completed the verification and determination, they concluded.
We have deeply benefited from the compassionate care of the Court Physician. Last year,
when we two monks were in Taizhou...
He received the precepts of both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna vehicles.
Furthermore, he transcribed several hundred scrolls of scriptures.
This year, he proceeded to Yuefu.
The two monks entered the five-section initiation mandala.
Furthermore, they transcribed the dharma-gates for recitation,
totaling two hundred and thirty works in all.
The work consists of four hundred and sixty fascicles.
Having completed this task,
I am now returning to my native province and wish to request an official seal from the local government.
This serves to demonstrate the fundamental origins of seeking the Dharma for the disciples from foreign lands. Thus,
it is the merit of the Langzhong in transmitting the Dharma.
One clings to blessings in the present and future lives;
through the merit of sentient beings listening to the Dharma,
one aspires for the fruit of wondrous enlightenment.
I humbly pray that you, Excellency,
may soon ascend to the rank of the Three Dukes and ultimately realize the fruit of the Three Points.
Thereupon, vertically they penetrate the three realms,
and horizontally they sweep across the ten directions.
May all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth enter the gate of dhyāna together and roam the garden of wisdom as one.
Faith and slander are equal;
do they not both bring benefit to oneself and others?

On the thirteenth day, the *xinsi* day, of the fifth month in the twenty-first year of the Zhenyuan era of the Great Tang (the year of *yǒuyǒu*, *yǐyou*), the Japanese monk seeking the Dharma, Saichō, recorded this, together with the Japanese monk translating and interpreting the Dharma, Gishin, and the Japanese attendant to the seeker of the Dharma, Fūjō. As Confucius said: [text follows].
I have heard that there is a sage in the West whose teaching takes purity and non-action as its foundation.
To be unstained and unattached is the sublime.
In transforming others,
he is fully endowed with merit and virtue.
Thus, he attained perfect enlightenment.
The Acharya Saichō was endowed by nature with the talent of innate wisdom.
Coming from a land of ritual and righteousness,
he sought the Dharma from ten thousand li away,
regarding perilous paths as if they were level plains.
Undaunted by hardship and toil,
he was protected by his supernatural powers as he ascended to the summit of Mount Tiantai.
To the west, he traversed the waters of Mirror Lake,
exhausting the Dharma-gates of the Wise One and exploring the mysteries of the Consecration (Abhiṣeka).
He may truly be called a dragon-elephant among the Dharma-gates;
like a blue lotus emerging from its pond,
he shall take this Mahāyāna and transmit it to his native land.
Seeking this seal of authentication to hold as a warrant,
I have already recorded it in writing for Lu Taizhou yesterday; therefore,
I set forth what I have observed here to submit in accordance with the direct pen.
Written on the fifteenth day of the fifth month in the twenty-first year of the Zhenyuan era of the Great Tang by Zheng Shenze,
Court Consultant, Commissioner with Authority over the Military Affairs of Mingzhou, Acting Governor of Mingzhou, and Marquis of Xingyang.
Japanese Envoy to Tang China:
Bian, concurrently Governor of Etchū Province;
Fujwara no Asomi Katsuno Makasa; Your Servant, Tasa.
The Six Ranks of the Great Officials of the Seishi [Office]:
Sanyama no Tsuko, Ōba no Sukune, Ushimodono no Kō, and Kashin no Sukune.
Preface to the Catalogue of the Mountain Home Transmitted by Shōnin: In the past, when our Three Sages entered Tang China to seek the Dharma...
There already exists a future record that was previously published in the world.
Now, this transcription has once again been specially preserved for longevity.
This was intended to ensure that his true calligraphic legacy remains imperishable.
Indeed, the flourishing state of culture and arts under our present dynasty is such that both the monastic robes and the lay garments are filled with its influence.
There has been no era greater than the sacred reigns of Enryaku and Kōnin;
as for the exquisite subtlety of his calligraphy,
even the masters of script from the late Tang dynasty onward could truly not have surpassed it.
Everyone was aware of this.
A person of Song praised him, saying, "He was almost equal to the two kings; this is no exaggeration.
Even at that time, such was the case.
How much more so for those who now exist in this world with several thousand characters;
these may truly be called rare treasures of the age.
Nevertheless, they must be preserved within the treasury of the mind.
Thus, it is not only that such people are rare;
I fear that perhaps this work may not remain intact for future generations.
How could one not feel regret over this?
In this summer of the year Xin-si,
the Venerable Fachuan Chugong brought a copy of the text by Guo Tian and said:
"It has been exactly one thousand years since the Great Master entered parinirvāṇa."
Today, the true original remains clearly visible.
Now that it has been carved and placed within the courtyard of the Kaifeng Pagoda, its transmission will endure for all eternity; how magnificent it is to behold!
At this, we all nodded our assent with a mere snap of the fingers.
Recently, the carving of the woodblocks was completed;
as fellow practitioners, we earnestly requested a single word as a preface.
I firmly declined, but was not permitted [to do so].
Therefore, disregarding all else, I have recorded the beginning and end of this matter in plain prose rather than literary style.
Written on the day of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony for the monastics in the year of *Bunkyū* (1841).
Compiled and written by the monk Ryōshō of Enryaku-ji, Channa-gō-bikku.
